result.title: Compression Forcing: Hierarchical History Tokenization Enables Flexible World Models
result.summary: Effective world modeling requires compressing salient history information that facilitates future prediction. However, most existing approaches inherit tokenization and conditioning mechanisms from video generation, where objectives are centered around perceptual realism rather than predictive utility. This discrepancy limits the world model's effectiveness, especially in environments dominated by visual nuisances or task-irrelevant background details. To this end, we introduce Compression Forcing (CF), a general framework that aligns history compression with the predictive objective of world modeling. Compression Forcing features Dynamics-Aware Tokenization (DAT), a novel tokenization method that compresses history observations into a sequence ordered by decreasing dynamics saliency. Built on a diffusion backbone, this structure enables Hierarchical History Guidance (HG-H), allowing selective amplification of dynamics-salient information during inference. Extensive experiments across various environments demonstrate improved prediction fidelity, physical realism, and downstream decision-making performance, establishing Compression Forcing as a highly flexible and effective approach for world modeling.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Compression Forcing 框架，用 Dynamics-Aware Tokenization 把历史观测压缩成按动态显著性递减排列的 token 序列，并在扩散骨干上以 Hierarchical History Guidance 在推理阶段选择性放大动态显著信息，以提升预测保真度与下游决策表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按预测效用而非感知真实感筛选历史视觉信息、并对压缩后的 token 做层级加权调用的设计，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、必要细节在 latent 中的保留及推理期动态调用 latent 内容有方法层面的呼应，可供核查，但该文面向世界模型预测而非多模态推理。
